docs.text: 1 Run a method Run Run a method Drive any of 40+ integration methods through one typed API, each in its own environment. Evaluate Evaluate a run Score a run output with scIB batch-correction, biological-conservation, and task-specific metrics. Plot Plot results Load published results into tidy frames and render scIB-style bubble plots and rankings. Explore Interactive explorer Browse benchmark results, metrics, rankings, and bubble tables in the Shiny explorer. 40+ methods, one API Run integration methods across four scenarios, vertical, diagonal, mosaic, and cross, through the typed multibench API. Each method runs in its own conda env, so their conflicting toolchains never collide. Metrics you can trust Each task gets its own metric panel, scIB batch-correction and biological-conservation scores, classification accuracy and F1, marker overlap, RMSE, plus runtime and peak memory, aggregated into per-method grand rank scores. Choose with evidence No single method wins everywhere. Explore rankings, bubble tables, and a decision tree that recommends top methods per scenario and task, so method choice is grounded in your data, not folklore.

docs.title: scMultiBench
docs.text:
A systematic benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration. Run 40+ integration methods through one typed Python API, score them with scIB and task-specific metrics, and explore the rankings to pick the right method for your data. 

pip install multibench-sc

Get started How it works

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The scMultiBench API (imported as multibench, aliased throughout the docs as mtb) exposes a small, flat, free-function API organised into a handful of namespaces:

  • mtb.* - the top-level surface: the benchmark workflow (scan, run_all, describe_layout), run one method, evaluate an output, to_long to reshape it, stored results (load_results, results_coverage, recommend), and discovery helpers (list_methods, find_methods, method_info, cite, inputs_for, labels_for). mtb.__all__ is exactly this surface (dir(mtb) shows nothing else); the 0.2.1 spellings are listed under Deprecated in 0.3.0.
  • mtb.plot.* - scIB-style figures (bubble, bar, build_table).
  • mtb.eval.* - the evaluation pipeline (evaluate, to_long).
  • mtb.io.* - the canonical-format adapter (export_dataset, to_canonical, read_canonical, normalize_peak_names).
  • mtb.data.* - fetch the reference datasets, fetch_outputs the benchmark host's run_all output trees for the tutorial datasets.
  • mtb.catalog.* - typed views of the benchmark's metadata tables.
  • mtb.config.* - resolved paths and knobs (Config, DEFAULT: data_path, envs_dir, leiden_flavor ...).
  • mtb.env.* - per-method environments: status, plan, install, doctor, recipe, and the run modes (env_prefix, MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE).

Backend and seed noise in the sweep metrics

ARI / NMI come from scIB's optimal-resolution Leiden sweep, and that sweep is noisy by construction. Measured on the tutorial datasets' real embeddings (7 methods, D11 / D28 / D46): two leidenalg seeds differ by up to 0.089 ARI on the same embedding, and the igraph backend differs from leidenalg by up to 0.097 ARI (mean 0.03) - the same magnitude. Running igraph to convergence (n_iterations=-1) does not narrow the gap, so the package keeps scanpy's documented two iterations. The speed difference is large: 0.3 s vs 9 s on 2.9k cells, 2 s vs 42-95 s on 11k cells. Treat differences below ~0.1 ARI between two runs, backends or seeds as noise; mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "leidenalg" selects the backend the published tables were computed with, and a scanpy older than 1.10 falls back to it automatically (one warning).

The end-to-end story: mtb.io.export_dataset writes your data as a dataset folder, mtb.scan says which methods can run on it, mtb.run_all runs and scores them into a BatchResult whose .long frame - the same tidy frame mtb.load_results returns for the stored benchmark - goes into mtb.plot.bubble. Underneath, mtb.run returns a RunResult whose output flows into mtb.evaluate, and mtb.to_long reshapes that into the same long frame. The same story from the shell:

terminal
multibench layout vertical                         # how to lay out MY data
multibench convert my.h5ad data/MYCITE --rna X --adt obsm:protein --labels obs:celltype
multibench scan MYCITE --category vertical --data-path data
multibench params Matilda                          # the hyperparameters --param accepts, per variant
multibench run --method Matilda --category vertical --input rna=... --out-dir runs/Matilda
multibench evaluate --output runs/Matilda/embedding.h5 --labels data/MYCITE/cty.csv \
    --method Matilda --dataset MYCITE --category vertical --out runs/Matilda/long.csv
multibench plot bubble --category vertical --dataset D11 --out fig.pdf
multibench plot bubble --input runs/Matilda/long.csv --category vertical --dataset D11 --out fig.pdf   # overlay
multibench cite Matilda MOFA2

Every subcommand wraps exactly one Python function with the same flag names; multibench <command> --help documents every flag. Tables, ids and commands go to stdout; progress ([run_all] ...), # dry run notes, warning: ... and error: ... go to stderr, so 2>/dev/null silences the chatter. scan and run-all --dry-run print the same frame as a compact table (method, modalities, runnable, files_ok, env_ok, runtime_tier, reason, long text clipped to 80 chars); --columns all or --format csv|tsv|json gives every column unclipped, command included - the exact command line run() would execute per variant whose inputs resolve (paths absolutized, exactly as run passes them; run-all --dry-run also lists them under the table). run --dry-run prints the one command (mtb.run(..., dry_run=True)), --param/-p METHOD:KEY=VALUE (KEY=VALUE on run) sets hyperparameters and params METHOD lists them per variant with the values the script pins. evaluate --metrics takes a family token or a comma list (--only is a hidden deprecated alias that prints warning: --only is deprecated since 0.3.0; use --metrics on stderr). plot --input is repeatable and, together with --category, overlays your rows on the stored table; convert takes --category (the ATAC filename rule) and copies an already-canonical .h5 instead of re-encoding it. The env commands are dry runs until --run, print a warning: ... linux-64 line on a non-Linux host, and env install --run refuses there unless --force. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a runtime error (error: ... on stderr; MULTIBENCH_DEBUG=1 shows the traceback), 2 a usage error.

Method environments

Running a method shells out to the environment it shares with other compatible tools, <env> = mtb.method_info(method)["env"] - the same env multibench env install / mtb.env.install provisions. The wrapper is chosen per call: when the env prefix <envs_dir>/<env> is on disk (a packed archive unpacked there - no conda binary needed) a bash -c line activates it and execs the command; otherwise conda run -n <env> <cmd>. See Run modes; cmd_template overrides both. The original method scripts are never modified - multibench only builds the command, converts inputs to the canonical .h5, and loads the typed output.

Error vocabulary

Every entry point validates its tokens the same way: an unknown method id raises KeyError with a did-you-mean hint; an unknown category, task, atac or modality token raises ValueError listing the valid values; a bare string where a list of ids / tokens is expected (methods="StabMap", modalities="rna") raises TypeError showing the list form; a missing dataset folder or file raises FileNotFoundError listing the folders that exist (or the path and the current directory); a method with several variants that neither modalities= nor the folder's files single out raises mtb.AmbiguousVariantError - a ValueError that also matches KeyError, listing the modality-sets and the folder's contents; a missing conda env raises OSError naming the install command. Warnings are UserWarnings, one of them a subclass you can filter on: mtb.DegenerateRerunWarning (a re-run row that most likely failed silently). Nothing silently returns an empty result.

docs.title: Benchmark workflow
docs.text: The four category tutorials are built on these functions.

docs.title: mtb.scan
docs.text:
mtb.scan(dataset: str, category: str | None = None, *, methods: list[str] | None = None,
         modalities: list[str] | None = None, data_path: Path | str | None = None,
         out_dir="<out_dir>", params: dict | None = None, verbose: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame

Report every method that can run on dataset, why the rest cannot, and the exact command each one would run - the frame run_all(..., dry_run=True) returns (identical, pinned by a test) and multibench scan / run-all --dry-run print. One row per (method, category, modalities) variant, runnable rows first, with two independent gates:

  • files_ok / files_reason - the input files resolve on disk, are oriented features x cells, every label CSV has one row per cell of the modality it labels, and a data_dir method finds what it needs (>= 2 .h5ad slices with obsm['spatial'] for registration). This gate always runs, whether or not any conda env is installed - a laptop without environments still tells you whether your layout is right.
  • env_ok / env_reason - the method's conda env exists on this machine; the reason names the env and the one-method install command. A method whose script calls CUDA unconditionally (method_info(m)["requires_gpu"]) also needs mtb.env.host_has_gpu() to be True; otherwise env_reason carries the sentence run would raise (<method> needs an NVIDIA GPU: the upstream script calls CUDA unconditionally (<file>:<line>); ...), joined after the install hint when the env is missing too. See GPU or CPU?.

runnable = files_ok & env_ok; reason joins the non-empty reasons (empty iff runnable) in a SHORT form - the exception class, the method/dataset/category: prefix and the absolute directory are dropped (input files not found on disk: {'atac': 'atac.h5'}. Available files in D11: [...]), while files_reason / env_reason keep the verbatim text with full paths. Further columns: modalities (a +-joined string here, e.g. "rna+adt"; run_all / inputs_for take a list - split on "+"; "(data_dir)" marks a method that consumes a whole directory), env, output_kind, n_tunable, needs_labels (does this variant demand a label file), atac ('peak' / 'gene_activity' / None), runtime_tier / observed_worst_sec (measured, see method_info(m)["runtime"] under method_info), caveat (known content traps: an ATAC role resolved to the wrong representation in either direction - a peak matrix fed to a gene-activity method, or a non-peak matrix fed to a peak method - judged per role from method_info(m)["atac"]) and command - the exact shell line run() would execute for that variant, built with run(..., dry_run=True) (paths absolutized exactly as run passes them; the empty string for a row whose inputs do not resolve). The frame has 18 columns: method, category, modalities, env, output_kind, n_tunable, runtime_tier, observed_worst_sec, caveat, runnable, reason, files_ok, files_reason, env_ok, env_reason, needs_labels, atac, command. The one method whose script is not published - SPIRAL, method_info(m)["availability"] == "benchmark-host-only" - fails the file gate with files_reason benchmark-host-only: script not published: .... GPSA ships as a package driver and is public. Nothing is executed and nothing is fetched or written.

>>> sc = mtb.scan("D11", "vertical")
[scan] files OK for 14/25 method rows; 0/25 envs installed
>>> sc.columns.tolist()
['method', 'category', 'modalities', 'env', 'output_kind', 'n_tunable', 'runtime_tier',
 'observed_worst_sec', 'caveat', 'runnable', 'reason', 'files_ok', 'files_reason',
 'env_ok', 'env_reason', 'needs_labels', 'atac', 'command']
>>> sc.command.iloc[0]
"conda run -n scmb_concerto python .../tools_scripts/Concerto/main_Concerto.py --path1 .../D11/rna.h5 --path2 .../D11/adt.h5 --save_path '.../<out_dir>/Concerto_D11/'"

command is the real line for THIS host: conda run -n <env> ... as above when the env is not unpacked here, the prefix-activating bash -c '...; exec "$@"' -- python ... wrapper when <envs_dir>/<env> exists (see Run modes).

Parameters

  • dataset (str) - folder NAME under data_path (not a path); a missing folder raises FileNotFoundError listing the folders that do exist.
  • category (str | None) - restrict to one category (ValueError on a typo); default all four.
  • methods (list[str] | None, keyword-only) - restrict to these ids (KeyError with a hint on a typo; a bare string raises TypeError); blocked rows are kept with their reason. Never empty: ValueError (no <category> variant matches ...) when no variant of the requested methods exists under category.
  • modalities (list[str] | None, keyword-only) - restrict to one modality combination (["rna", "adt"]; protein accepted for adt; a bare string raises TypeError). An exact selector, so directory-input variants ("(data_dir)") are excluded by any non-empty list - a UserWarning names them and says modalities=[] selects exactly them.
  • data_path (Path | str | None, keyword-only) - the folder that CONTAINS dataset; default the configured data root.
  • out_dir (keyword-only) - the output directory the command lines name; the default is the literal placeholder <out_dir>, so a preview needs no directory - pass the real one for paste-ready lines.
  • params (dict | None, keyword-only) - per-method hyperparameters merged into the command lines ({"Matilda": {"epochs": 5}}); a key the method does not accept raises KeyError naming the accepted ones.
  • verbose (bool) - print [scan] files OK for k/n method rows; e/n envs installed (default True; the CLI passes False).

docs.title: mtb.run_all
docs.text:
mtb.run_all(dataset: str, category: str, out_dir=None, *, methods=None, modalities=None,
            params: dict | None = None, data_path=None, evaluate: bool = True,
            dry_run: bool = False, verbose: bool = True, timeout: float | None = None,
            skip_existing: bool = False, batch=None) -> BatchResult | pd.DataFrame

Run every method that scan marks runnable (or the methods= subset) on dataset end to end - inputs, the method's own conda env, output loading, metrics - and collect everything in a BatchResult. A method that fails becomes a row in .failures, never an exception. When nothing is runnable the ValueError lists one line per requested variant with its own reason (or the first 3 of N blocked variants when methods= was not given); a requested method with no variant in the category raises scan's no <category> variant matches ....

Parameters

  • dataset / data_path - as in scan.
  • out_dir - one sub-directory per method. Required for a real run (TypeError: run_all() needs out_dir= for a real run (dry_run=True returns the scan frame without one)); may be omitted with dry_run=True.
  • methods (list[str] | None) - restrict to these ids (KeyError + hint on a typo).
  • modalities (list[str] | None) - restrict to ONE modality combination, e.g. ["rna", "atac_gas"] (gene activity) vs ["rna", "atac_peak"] (peaks). The two ATAC representations do NOT map to the obvious filenames - see describe_layout.
  • params (dict | None) - per-method hyperparameters, {"Cobolt": {"lr": 1e-3}}; discover them with params_for (--param/-p METHOD:KEY=VALUE on the command line). An unknown method id raises KeyError before any I/O; with dry_run=True a key the method does not accept raises too, naming the accepted ones (a real run records it as that method's FAIL row).
  • dry_run (bool) - return scan(...) for the same selection - the identical frame, command column included - without running anything. Free; do it first.
  • timeout (float | None) - per-method wall-clock cap in seconds; size it from scan's runtime_tier / observed_worst_sec. A method exceeding it is recorded as TIMEOUT and the sweep moves on.
  • skip_existing (bool) - reuse a method's existing output file instead of recomputing (resume an interrupted sweep). Together with params= it raises ValueError - reuse is keyed on the file, not the parameters. Reuse only checks that the file exists, not that it is complete.
  • batch (keyword-only) - one batch id per cell, in the embedding's row order (array-like / Series / CSV path), used for the batch metrics INSTEAD of the default rule (batch = the label FILE each cell came from, cty1.csv -> 1 ...). Recorded as batch_source='user'; a wrong length marks that method RUN_OK_EVAL_FAILED.
  • evaluate (bool) - compute metrics on the outputs (default True); verbose - per-method progress lines.

docs.title: BatchResult
docs.text:
What run_all returns (and load_batch reloads).

  • .summary - one row per method, sorted by method name: method, status, run_sec, output_kind, emb_shape, n_tunable, label_order, label_order_confidence, batch_source, n_batches plus one column per metric. status is CHAIN_OK, CHAIN_OK_GRAPH_METHOD, RUN_OK_NO_EMBEDDING, RUN_OK_EVAL_FAILED, TIMEOUT or FAIL; batch_source is file_of_origin (the label-file rule), user (batch= / rescore) or None (single label file).
  • .long - the tidy seven-column metric, value, method, dataset, category, clustering, source frame (source="user"), the input to mtb.plot.bubble; a long.csv written by an earlier release reloads with the two columns filled.
  • .failures - method, status, error for everything that went wrong (always check it).
  • .results - the raw per-method records (status, out_dir, metrics, label_order_candidates), so a sweep's outputs stay addressable.
  • .plot(**kw) - bubble figure of every scored method; keywords go to plot.bubble (metrics=, methods=, order=, title=, save= ...). Raises ValueError if nothing scored.
  • .rescore(*, batch=None, labels=None, metrics=None, verbose=False) -> BatchResult - re-evaluate the STORED outputs with a different batch vector, labels or metric selection (metrics= as in evaluate) - nothing is re-run; returns a new BatchResult (call .save() to persist it).
  • .save(out_dir=None) -> Path - writes summary.csv, long.csv, failures.csv, batch_result.json (run_all does this automatically).

docs.title: mtb.load_batch
docs.text:
mtb.load_batch(out_dir, *, methods: list[str] | None = None) -> BatchResult

Reload a BatchResult that run_all / BatchResult.save wrote, to re-plot, re-inspect or rescore without re-running anything. methods (keyword-only) keeps only those methods' records - what the tutorials do with the benchmark host's output tree: mtb.load_batch(mtb.data.fetch_outputs("D11"), methods=["Matilda", "sciPENN", "scMM"]) (see fetch_outputs); None (the default) keeps every record, as before.

docs.title: mtb.params_for
docs.text:
mtb.params_for(method: str, category: str | None = None, modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None, *,
               dataset: str | None = None, data_path: Path | str | None = None) -> dict

The tunable hyperparameters a method's variant exposes (tunable, with defaults), the defaults the wrapper emits, the effective values a wrapper run uses, fixed_in_script (with file:line) and the upstream knobs the script never exposes. A multi-variant method needs modalities= (or category=) to pick the variant, or dataset= (+ data_path=): then the variant whose input files are all in that folder is chosen, and mtb.AmbiguousVariantError names the modality-sets when none or several are. modalities=["rna", "atac"] selects an atac_gas / atac_peak variant too. An empty tunable means the upstream script hardcodes its settings. multibench params METHOD [--category] [--modalities] [--format table|csv|tsv|json] prints the same per variant (all variants when none is selected).

docs.title: mtb.describe_layout
docs.text:
mtb.describe_layout(category: str | None = None) -> str

How to lay out your OWN dataset so the package can find it: the directory layout and the role -> filename mapping (rna.h5, adt.h5, atac.h5 / peak.h5, cty.csv, numbered rna1.h5 ... per batch), the HDF5 file format (matrix/data features x cells, matrix/features, matrix/barcodes), the ATAC peak-vs-gene-activity warning with the method lists built from the registry at call time, the export_dataset route, and - for cross - the SPATIAL REGISTRATION block (a directory of .h5ad slices). category is validated; 'spatial' raises with a pointer to describe_layout('cross').

docs.title: mtb.sweep
docs.text:
mtb.sweep(dataset: str, category: str, method: str, param: str, values, *,
          out_dir, modalities=None, data_path=None, timeout=None, verbose=True) -> pd.DataFrame

Run ONE method repeatedly over a range of one hyperparameter, one output directory per value, and return the per-setting metrics with the swept value as a column (a tidy frame goes to <out_dir>/sweep_long.csv, one series per setting, ready for plot.bubble). A failing setting appears with status FAIL / TIMEOUT rather than aborting the sweep.

docs.title: mtb.run
docs.text:
mtb.run(method: str, category: str, *, inputs: dict, out_dir: str, params: dict | None = None,
        task: str | None = None, convert: bool = True, cmd_template: str | None = None,
        repo_path: Path | None = None, dry_run: bool = False) -> RunResult | list[str]

Build a method variant's command, preflight its conda env, wrap the command (default "conda run -n {env} {cmd}"), run it in out_dir, and load the typed output. inputs is a {modality_role: path-or-AnnData} dict; non-canonical modality inputs are auto-converted to the canonical scMultiBench .h5 (into <out_dir>/inputs/) unless convert=False. Auxiliary roles (data_dir, source_data, target_data, source_cty, target_cty, out_dir) are passed through verbatim. Returns a RunResult, or the argv list with dry_run=True.

Parameters

  • method (str) - registry method id (KeyError with a did-you-mean hint otherwise).
  • category (str) - one of vertical, diagonal, mosaic, cross; drives variant selection together with the supplied modalities. Everything after it is keyword-only (a third positional argument raises TypeError).
  • inputs (dict) - {modality_role: path}, e.g. {"rna": ..., "atac_gas": ...}; the non-auxiliary, non-label roles select the variant. Paths may be relative: every path-valued input is made absolute (symlinks preserved) and a directory role such as data_dir gets its trailing separator before the argv is built, because the method runs with cwd=out_dir.
  • out_dir (str) - working directory; created if missing, made absolute the same way (RunResult.out_dir is the absolute path).
  • params (dict | None) - extra method hyperparameters merged into the command. On a host without an NVIDIA GPU the method's cpu_params (method_info(m)["cpu_params"], the flags that turn CUDA off - scJoint's --use_cuda "", scMDC's --device cpu) are merged in first, so a key given here wins; one line [run] no GPU on this host: applying <method> cpu_params {...} goes to stderr on a real run. See GPU or CPU?.
  • task (str | None) - accepted and currently ignored: variant selection depends only on category and the supplied modalities.
  • convert (bool) - convert non-aux inputs to the canonical .h5 (default True).
  • cmd_template (str | None) - command wrapper; None picks the run mode for the method's env - the prefix activation when <envs_dir>/<env> is on disk, else conda run -n {env} {cmd} - and preflights it (OSError naming the install command when the env is missing); a custom template overrides both and skips the preflight.
  • repo_path (Path | None) - checkout holding tools_scripts/; default auto-provisioned (config.DEFAULT.repo_path).
  • dry_run (bool) - return the wrapped argv (a list[str]) that a real call would execute - inputs absolutized as above, the checkout located but never fetched, nothing created or written, no env preflight. The form behind multibench run --dry-run and scan's command column; it shows the merged cpu_params and previews a requires_gpu method even on a GPU-less host.

Raises OSError before anything is written or launched when method_info(m)["requires_gpu"] is True and mtb.env.host_has_gpu() is False: <method> needs an NVIDIA GPU: the upstream script calls CUDA unconditionally (<file>:<line>); see method_info(m)["requires_gpu"] - the same sentence scan reports in env_reason.

>>> mtb.run("Matilda", "vertical", inputs=mtb.inputs_for("D11", "vertical", "Matilda"),
...         out_dir="out/Matilda", dry_run=True)[:6]                       # conda mode (no prefix on disk)
['conda', 'run', '-n', 'matilda', 'python', '.../multibench/engine/drivers/run_matilda.py']

With the matilda prefix unpacked under envs_dir the same call returns the prefix-mode argv, ['bash', '-c', '<activate>; exec "$@"', '--', 'python', ...].

docs.title: mtb.evaluate
docs.text:
mtb.evaluate(output, labels=None, *, category: str | None = None, batch=None, metrics=None,
             clustering=None, obsm: str = "X_emb", label_order=None, verbose: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame

Compute scIB metrics on a run output, returning a metric.csv-shaped frame (index = metric in the canonical spelling load_results uses, single Value column; never empty - a request that selects no metric raises). metrics= is the one selection knob (see the metrics= vocabulary): None computes every applicable metric - the clustering family, plus the batch family whenever a batch vector exists. ARI, NMI and iF1 need scIB's Leiden resolution sweep - the slow part: with the default mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "igraph" (scanpy's flavor="igraph", n_iterations=2, directed=False; measured 7.7x faster than "leidenalg" on 20k cells) seconds for ~10^4 cells, with "leidenalg" tens of seconds for a few thousand cells and minutes for ~10^4; one stderr line announces the sweep above 2,000 cells and names the flavor (verbose), and clustering= or a metrics=[...] list naming only metrics that do not need it skips it. Clustering metrics require labels; clustering is optional (omitted -> scIB optimal-resolution Leiden, ten resolutions 0.2-2.0, highest NMI). The batch family requires batch - unless labels is a list (or an ordered dict) of two or more files, in which case the file of origin is the batch (the run_all rule). batch= under metrics="clustering" computes no batch metric and emits a UserWarning. Everything after labels is keyword-only (the 0.2 positional evaluate(output, category, ...) raises TypeError). This is re-exported from mtb.eval.evaluate.

Parameters

  • output - the embedding, cells x dims: numpy.ndarray (dims x cells is auto-transposed against the label count, with a warning), pandas.DataFrame, AnnData (uses .obsm[obsm]), scipy sparse, or a path - .h5 (dataset data, the benchmark's embedding.h5), .h5ad (read as an AnnData, so its obs columns and ids are usable), .npy, .csv / .tsv. A missing path raises FileNotFoundError naming it and the current directory; an .h5 without data raises ValueError listing its keys (and says so when it looks like a canonical INPUT matrix). An AnnData (obs_names) or a DataFrame with a non-default index carries cell ids - see labels.
  • labels - one cell type per cell in the row order of output: a CSV path (header row; column x / the only column / the last of two behind a barcode index; a file with several columns is ambiguous - pass the column itself, pd.read_csv(p)["col"]), a LIST of CSV paths concatenated in order, a dict from labels_for (one entry, or several in the cell-stacking order labels_for returns; any other order needs label_order=), a 1-D array / Series / Categorical / list, a single-column DataFrame, or - for an AnnData output - an obs column name. Arrays, lists and files are matched POSITIONALLY; a Series / DataFrame with a non-default index is ALIGNED BY CELL ID when output carries ids (AnnData / indexed DataFrame) - missing or extra ids raise ValueError naming the first offenders - and matched positionally with a UserWarning against a bare array (labels.to_numpy() silences it).
  • category (str | None) - validated when given (ValueError listing the four); the metrics do not depend on it.
  • batch - batch labels, one per cell (same forms and alignment rule; obs column name for AnnData).
  • metrics - None (every applicable metric) | "clustering" | "batch" | "all" | a list of metric codes. A list computes exactly those (alias tolerant, ["ari", "nmi"] -> ARI, NMI) and skips everything else, including the Leiden sweep when no listed metric needs it (ARI, NMI and iF1 need it; clustering= replaces it for ARI / NMI); kBET is computed only when named in a list (R via rpy2; hours on large datasets). "all" or "batch" without a batch vector raises ValueError (batch labels required for metrics='all' ...: pass batch=<vector>, or metrics='clustering'), as does a listed batch metric; a bare code (metrics="ARI"), a list_tasks() token ("imputation"), an unknown code or an empty list raise ValueError naming the valid vocabulary.
  • clustering - optional precomputed cluster assignment (same forms and alignment rule as labels, obs column name for AnnData; an .h5 path is read from /obs/cluster_leiden); skips the Leiden sweep.
  • obsm (str) - .obsm key for AnnData / .h5ad output (default "X_emb"; "X" means .X).
  • label_order (list[str] | None) - only for a multi-entry labels dict: its keys in the order the method stacked the cells (numbered files ascending - cty1, cty2, ... - and rna before atac, NOT alphabetical; label_order=list(d) trusts a dict from labels_for). A subset of the keys selects those files; unknown / repeated / empty raise ValueError, label_order with non-dict labels raises TypeError.
  • verbose (bool) - True (default) prints the Leiden-sweep notice on stderr above 2,000 cells; False never prints.

Raises ValueError for missing labels / batch, unknown category or metric name, length mismatches (input length mismatch: emb has N cells, celltype has M), cell-id mismatches when aligning, ambiguous label files and a multi-entry dict in a non-stacking order without label_order; TypeError for unsupported input types and for the removed 0.2 keywords (see Deprecated in 0.3.0).

>>> mtb.evaluate(emb, labels).index.tolist()                      # single batch: the clustering family
['ARI', 'NMI', 'ASW', 'iASW', 'iF1', 'cLISI']
>>> mtb.evaluate(emb, labels, batch=batch).index.tolist()         # a batch vector: both families (kBET only when named)
['ARI', 'NMI', 'ASW', 'iASW', 'iF1', 'cLISI', 'ASW_batch', 'GC', 'iLISI']
>>> mtb.evaluate(emb, labels, metrics=["ASW"]).index.tolist()     # no Leiden sweep
['ASW']

Graceful degradation

Metrics whose external dependency is unavailable return NaN with a warning rather than failing the call: cLISI / iLISI need scib's compiled LISI helper, which ships as a Linux x86-64 binary - when it cannot run, evaluate rebuilds it in place once with scib's own build line if g++ / c++ / clang++ is on PATH, and only otherwise records NaN (the warning carries the g++ rebuild command); kBET needs R via rpy2 (and is computed only when metrics=[...] names it). All other scIB metrics (ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, ASW_batch, GC) compute in pure Python.

docs.title: The metrics= vocabulary
docs.text:
evaluate, load_results, recommend and BatchResult.rescore share one metric selector, parsed in one place:

metrics= selects None (default) every metric available / applicable: for evaluate, the clustering family plus the batch family when a batch vector exists; for load_results, every metric in the tables; for recommend, the clustering family "clustering" ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI (mtb.plot.CLUSTERING_METRICS) "batch" ASW_batch, GC, iLISI, kBET (mtb.plot.BATCH_METRICS) "all" both families (evaluate then needs a batch vector) a list of codes exactly those, alias tolerant (["ari", "nmi"]); evaluate computes kBET only this way

A bare code (metrics="ARI") raises ValueError pointing at the list form; a mtb.list_tasks() token ("imputation", "dimension_reduction") raises explaining that the slot selects a metric family; an unknown code raises listing the valid ones (['ARI', 'NMI', 'ASW', 'iASW', 'iF1', 'cLISI', 'ASW_batch', 'GC', 'iLISI', 'kBET', 'PCR']). It replaces the 0.2 task=, family=, only= and slow_metrics= keywords.

docs.title: mtb.to_long
docs.text:
mtb.to_long(value_df, *, method: str, dataset: str | None = None, category: str | None = None,
            clustering: str = "default", source: str = "user") -> pd.DataFrame

Reshape an evaluate wide frame (index = metric, column Value; a Series, or the CSV read back with a metric column, is accepted too) into the seven-column long frame metric, value, method, dataset, category, clustering, source that load_results and plot.bubble consume - source="user" keeps your rows distinguishable after a concat. method is required and keyword-only (to_long(df, "M", "D11", "vertical") raises TypeError); dataset=None writes all and category=None writes user, so no column is ever blank (a NaN dataset would vanish in the plot layer's groupby). A needs_labels column added by hand (long["needs_labels"] = True) is still honoured by plot.build_table and gives a method outside the registry the L badge. Metric codes are canonicalised (ari -> ARI, kbet -> kBET; evaluate already emits the canonical names, so its frames concatenate with load_results without duplicate metric columns); blank names are dropped, two rows that collapse onto the same canonical name raise ValueError (a silent duplicate would double-count that metric in every rank), an index where nothing canonicalises raises, and a frame that is already long or has no Value column is rejected with a message naming the shape (and the df.T.set_axis(["Value"], axis=1) fix). Also available as mtb.eval.to_long.

docs.title: mtb.load_results
docs.text:
mtb.load_results(category: str | None = None, *, dataset: str | list[str] | None = None,
                 methods: str | list[str] | None = None, metrics=None, clustering: str = "default",
                 source: str = "published", result_path: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

Benchmark metric tables as a tidy long frame with the columns, in this order, metric, value, method, dataset, category, clustering, source. Method ids are canonical registry tokens (MOFA+ -> MOFA2, Seurat(WNN) -> Seurat_WNN) and metric codes canonical (iFI -> iF1). When the default-clustering correction file metric_asw_iasw_if1.csv is present, its corrected ASW / iASW / iF1 values override those in metric.csv.

Parameters

  • category (str | None) - vertical, diagonal, mosaic, or cross; None loads every category that has tables for source (ValueError on an unknown token). The only positional parameter - every selector below is keyword-only.
  • dataset (str | list[str] | None) - dataset id(s); default all of the category. Every element is validated: a dataset with no table raises FileNotFoundError naming the missing ids and the available ones (across both sources for "both").
  • methods (str | list[str] | None) - keep only these methods (alias tolerant, case-folded against the registry); an id the registry does not know raises KeyError with a did-you-mean hint, a known method with no rows gives an empty frame plus a UserWarning listing the methods present (and the source that has it).
  • metrics - None (every metric in the tables) | "clustering" | "batch" | "all" | a list of codes (alias tolerant; same empty-frame rule) - the shared vocabulary.
  • clustering (str) - default, louvain, or kmeans (metric.csv / metric_louvain.csv / metric_kmeans.csv). A <method>_louvain result dir is reported under the canonical id with clustering="louvain"; a table kept one level down in a run-configuration folder (MOFA2/filtered3/metric.csv, MOFA2/kmeans/metric_kmeans.csv - cross D53 / D56 / D57) is read too (kbet/ skipped, an ambiguity warned). The re-run sweeps are default only.
  • source (str) - "published" (default; the paper's scIB tables - none for mosaic), "rerun" (the package's sweeps rerun/long_all_<dataset>.csv: vertical D11/D11s, diagonal D28/D28s, mosaic D45/D45s, cross D52/D52s; the source column says rerun, the sweep's package version travels in frame.attrs["rerun_version"]), or "both". Loading rerun / both emits mtb.DegenerateRerunWarning (a UserWarning) for a re-run row whose ARI is below 0.01 where the published table scored above 0.2 for the same (category, dataset, method) - computed at load time, today Conos on D28 - with the line to drop it before ranking.
  • result_path (Path | str | None) - a results ROOT (holding scib_metric/ and/or rerun/; default the tables shipped in the package) OR a single long CSV file: blank clustering / source cells are filled per row (default / user), source="published" or "both" keeps every row, and any other source value filters on the file's own column (a value the file does not carry raises ValueError listing the ones present).

Raises FileNotFoundError (no table for the request, with the path looked at and what IS available - mosaic says "use source='rerun'"), ValueError (unknown category / metrics / clustering / source, or a result_path file without the long-format columns).

>>> mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", metrics="batch").metric.unique()
array(['GC', 'iLISI', 'kBET', 'ASW_batch'], dtype=object)

docs.title: mtb.available_datasets
docs.text:
mtb.available_datasets(category: str | None = None, *, source: str = "published",
                       result_path: Path | str | None = None) -> list[str]

The dataset ids that have a stored default-clustering table for category / source - exactly what load_results can load ([] with a warning when the root is absent); published: vertical 23, diagonal 18, cross 7 (D52-D54, D56-D59), mosaic none - 48 in all. These are ids with stored tables, not downloads: the datasets mtb.data.fetch can download are the five reference sets D11, D28, D45, D46, D52 (mtb.data.fetchable(); any other id raises ValueError naming them).

docs.title: mtb.results_coverage
docs.text:
mtb.results_coverage(category: str | None = None, *, source: str = "both",
                     result_path: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

Which (category, dataset, method, clustering, source) combinations have results, one row each, sorted - the published tree is scanned for every clustering variant. A category without tables simply has no rows.

docs.title: mtb.recommend
docs.text:
mtb.recommend(category: str, *, modalities: list[str] | None = None,
              methods: list[str] | None = None, metrics=None, long_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
              min_methods: int = 2, source: str = "published",
              result_path: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

Rank methods for a category from stored results, best first, with coverage made explicit: columns method, grand_score, n_datasets, n_datasets_total, coverage, needs_labels, runtime_tier, worst_sec, env, output_kind. The score is the benchmark's own rule per dataset (overall="mean_overall": min-max scaled mean of per-metric max-ranks, averaged over the datasets the method was run on); datasets with fewer than min_methods methods are DROPPED (a lone method's min-max is 1.0 by construction). Every method wired for the category (find_methods(category, modalities=, runnable=True)) that has no rows in the chosen source is appended after the scored rows with grand_score NaN, n_datasets 0 and coverage 0.0, and ONE multi-line UserWarning lists the dropped datasets, the partial coverage and the unscored methods (suggesting source="rerun" when that source has them); frame.attrs records the choices the ranking was made under (metrics, family, source, not_scored, missing, dropped_methods, unranked_registration - pandas keeps .attrs through .copy() and column selection but most concat / merge operations drop them, so the NaN rows are the robust signal). modalities keeps methods consuming ALL of them (via find_methods); methods restricts the ranking to these ids; metrics is the shared selector - None ranks on the clustering family (today's default), "batch" on the batch-correction family, "all" or a list on exactly those; long_df scores your own frame (pd.concat([published, mine])) instead of loading. Inherits DegenerateRerunWarning from load_results. Raises ValueError when nothing can be ranked (also when the chosen family has no rows in the frame), FileNotFoundError when no stored results exist for the category / source.

docs.title: mtb.list_methods
docs.text:
mtb.list_methods(category: str | None = None) -> list[str]

Return the registry method ids, optionally filtered to those declaring a given category. A method's categories are derived from its variants (the registry refuses a separate categories: key), so list_methods, find_methods and env plan --category agree: 18 vertical, 14 diagonal, 6 mosaic, 12 cross, 40 in all. category is its only parameter: list_methods(task=...) / (runnable=...) raise TypeError (list_methods() only takes category since 0.3.0; task=... are find_methods filters - use find_methods(category, task=...)) - inspect.signature shows a **_removed catch-all that exists only to produce that message.

docs.title: mtb.list_tasks
docs.text:
mtb.list_tasks() -> list[str]
# ['batch', 'classification', 'clustering', 'dimension_reduction', 'imputation', 'registration']

Return the sorted set of tasks declared across all method specs.

docs.title: mtb.find_methods
docs.text:
mtb.find_methods(category: str | None = None, *, task: str | None = None,
                 needs_labels: bool | None = None, atac: str | None = None,
                 modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None, runnable: bool | None = None,
                 tunable: bool | None = None, available: bool | None = None) -> list[str]

Return method ids matching every supplied filter. category is the only positional parameter; every other filter is keyword-only (find_methods("vertical", "clustering") raises TypeError). Every token is validated: a typo raises ValueError naming the valid vocabulary instead of silently matching nothing. category, modalities, needs_labels and atac are evaluated per variant: a method matches when ONE of its variants satisfies all of them together - so scMoMaT is listed for find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"], needs_labels=False) (its vertical variant takes no labels, only its mosaic one does) and Multigrate is not listed for find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "atac"]) (its only ATAC-consuming variant is mosaic).

Parameters

  • category (str | None) - integration category the method must declare.
  • task (str | None) - one of list_tasks (find_methods("diagonal", task="clustering") - the 0.2 list_methods(task=)).
  • needs_labels (bool | None) - per variant: does the matching variant take a cell-type-label (cty) role as a REQUIRED input (method_info(m)["supports"][i]["needs_labels"]); method_info(m)["needs_labels"] is the any-variant flag.
  • atac (str | None) - exact match on the declared ATAC representation, "peak" or "gene_activity" (aliases "peaks" / "gas") - what the UPSTREAM script expects, which is not always what its role name suggests (moETM / scMM / iPOLNG take role atac_gas but consume peaks); only variants that consume ATAC can satisfy it.
  • modalities (list[str] | set[str] | None) - keep methods that consume ALL of these base modality types (["rna", "atac"]); "protein" is accepted for adt and role tokens (atac_gas, rna1 ...) are reduced to their base type; a bare string raises TypeError showing the list form. Implicitly excludes stub methods without variants. Methods that take a whole directory (data_dir: the four registration methods) cannot be judged and are KEPT with a UserWarning naming them; scBridge's modalities come from the bare filenames it reads (rna, atac).
  • runnable (bool | None) - True: methods with at least one variant; False: only the stubs.
  • tunable (bool | None) - True: only methods exposing at least one hyperparameter on their command line.
  • available (bool | None, keyword-only) - True: only methods a public install can run (method_info(m)["availability"] == "public", GPSA included - it runs through a package driver); False: the one whose script is not published, SPIRAL (benchmark-host-only).

docs.title: mtb.method_info
docs.text:
mtb.method_info(method: str, *, verbose: bool = False) -> dict

A flat dict combining the registry spec with the method's provenance. Keys: id, language, categories, tasks, env, atac, needs_labels (the METHOD-level flag: any variant takes a cty role - per variant read supports[i]["needs_labels"]), status (verified = the command template was cross-checked against the upstream entrypoint AND executed end to end on a reference dataset; declared = wired, not run), availability (public - every entrypoint lives in the public scMultiBench repository - or benchmark-host-only - an entrypoint is an absolute path on the benchmark host and is not published: SPIRAL; scan reports it not runnable. GPSA runs through the package driver engine/drivers/run_gpsa.py and is public), setup_hint, variants (distinct upstream entrypoints), driver (package-side wrapper, or None), scripts_url, repo_url, version, reference ({doi, title, authors, journal, year} or None), notes (short summary), supports (per variant: category, modalities, output_kind, n_tunable, needs_labels), params (per variant: defaults, tunable, effective), fixed_in_script, upstream_knobs, upstream_url, runtime (below) and the GPU/CPU contract of the upstream script - cpu_params ({} for most methods; {'use_cuda': ''} for scJoint, {'device': 'cpu'} for scMDC: the command-line values that turn CUDA off, merged by run on a GPU-less host), requires_gpu (True when the script calls CUDA unconditionally - scBridge, moETM, SMILE, sciCAN, UnitedNet, iPOLNG, SPIRAL - so run refuses it and scan reports env_ok=False without a GPU) and gpu_evidence (the file:line of that call, else None); see GPU or CPU?. env is the conda env run executes in - the {env} of the default cmd_template, the env column of scan and the name env doctor / env recipe use - e.g. scmb_torch for SCALEX, scmb_cobolt3 for Cobolt, matilda for Matilda. verbose=True adds notes_long (the upstream-knob audit prose; for a host-only method one sentence says why) and verification - the evidence behind status="verified": a list of {dataset, category, status, wall_s, ARI, baseline, verdict, note} read from the shipped multibench/files/final_verification.tsv (None when no run is recorded; also mtb.discover.verification_for(m)). There status is the run outcome (CHAIN_OK = ran and its embedding was scored, CHAIN_OK_GRAPH_METHOD = graph output scored via its UMAP, RUN_OK_NO_EMBEDDING = ran, output is not an embedding - registration methods), baseline the ARI at first verification and verdict OK or DRIFT (a stochastic re-run left the tolerance). The catalog columns (deep_learning, output) live in mtb.catalog.methods(); files_dir= is gone (TypeError).

method_info(m)["runtime"] - what the method has been OBSERVED to cost (the 0.2 runtime_hint(m) dict, unchanged): {"tier", "worst_sec", "observed"} - tier in fast (<5 min), medium (5-30 min), slow (30 min-2 h), very_slow (>2 h); observed lists the actual measurements on one shared machine as {dataset, cells, sec, source}, where source says where the number came from (manual, summary_csv = the shipped re-run sweeps, verification = the shipped verification table) - the table keeps the longest time recorded per (method, dataset), rounded up, and cells is null where no run recorded the count. A never-measured method has tier "unknown". It is the source of scan's runtime_tier / observed_worst_sec and recommend's runtime_tier / worst_sec; use it to size run_all(timeout=...), not to promise a finish time.

>>> mtb.method_info("SCALEX")["runtime"]
{'observed': [{'cells': 11014, 'dataset': 'D28', 'sec': 2233, 'source': 'manual'}], 'tier': 'slow', 'worst_sec': 2233}

docs.title: mtb.cite
docs.text:
mtb.cite(*methods, fmt: str = "text") -> str

Citation text: the benchmark entry first, then one entry per method in the order given. Ids go one per argument (cite("Matilda", "MOFA2"), like multibench cite Matilda MOFA2) or as one list (cite(["Matilda", "MOFA2"]), so cite(res.summary.method) works after a sweep); nothing -> the benchmark only; "all" -> every registry method; KeyError + hint on a typo. The 0.2 methods= keyword and the positional cite([ids], "bibtex") form raise TypeError. Methods whose DOI is not yet curated are emitted as a comment naming their repository, never silently dropped. fmt is "text" (default; one "Authors. Title. Journal (year). https://doi.org/..." line each) or "bibtex" (one @article per entry - the CLI's default). Every DOI was resolved against Crossref.

>>> print(mtb.cite())
Liu C, Ding S, Kim HJ, Long S, Xiao D, Ghazanfar S, Yang P. Multitask benchmarking of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods. Nature Methods (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02856-3

docs.title: mtb.inputs_for
docs.text:
mtb.inputs_for(dataset: str, category: str, method: str, *,
               modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None, data_path: Path | str | None = None,
               check: bool | None = False) -> dict

Resolve a dataset folder + method to concrete {modality_role: path} input paths. The positional order is (dataset, category, method) - the same as scan / run_all - and the 0.2 order is refused, never silently accepted: inputs_for("D11", "Matilda", "vertical") raises TypeError (inputs_for argument order is (dataset, category, method) since 0.3.0; you passed (dataset, method, category)). The dataset tree is flat (<data_path>/<dataset>/<file>); each role is resolved to the file actually present - the role token or a known alias (atac_peak -> peak.h5, atac_gas -> atac.h5), falling back to <role>.h5. Every returned path is absolute (a relative data_path is resolved against the current directory). When modalities is omitted and the method has exactly one variant for the category, that variant is used; with several, the one whose input files are all in the folder is chosen; when none or several are, mtb.AmbiguousVariantError (a ValueError) lists the modality-sets, the folder's contents and an example modalities=. modalities=["rna", "atac"] (or gas / peak) selects a variant declared atac_gas / atac_peak too. Use labels_for for the cell-type label files.

Parameters

  • dataset (str) - dataset folder name under data_path (e.g. "D28").
  • category (str) - integration category (validated).
  • method (str) - registry method id.
  • modalities (list[str] | set[str] | None, keyword-only) - exact modality-set to select a variant (protein accepted for adt).
  • data_path (Path | str | None, keyword-only) - override config.DEFAULT.data_path.
  • check (bool | None, keyword-only) - False (default): return the resolved paths silently, whether or not they exist; None: warn about missing ones (UserWarning naming them); True: raise FileNotFoundError (listing what IS in the folder) and also run the content preflight - matrix orientation (ValueError for a cells x features file), label length (one row per cell of the modality it labels), and the data_dir content check - exactly what scan reports as files_ok / files_reason.
>>> mtb.inputs_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX")
{'rna': '.../data/D28/rna.h5', 'atac_gas': '.../data/D28/atac_gas.h5'}

docs.title: mtb.labels_for
docs.text:
mtb.labels_for(dataset: str, category: str | None = None, method: str | None = None, *,
               modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None, data_path: Path | str | None = None) -> dict

Return {name: path} of the cell-type label CSVs for a dataset - the *cty*.csv files in the (flat) dataset directory, under their dataset-specific names (cty.csv, rna_cty.csv, cty1.csv, ...), excluding tool-specific *_scjoint* reformats - in the benchmark's cell-stacking order, not alphabetical: cty first; numbered cty1, cty2, ..., cty10 ascending numerically; modality-named files as rna_cty, adt_cty, atac_cty (peak_cty counts as atac - the diagonal methods emit the RNA cells, then the ATAC cells, so D28 gives {'rna_cty', 'atac_cty'}); anything else last. When category AND method are given - the same (dataset, category, method) order as inputs_for; labels_for("D11", "Matilda", "vertical") raises the same old-order TypeError, and a path in the category slot raises TypeError (pass data_path= by keyword) - the files follow that variant's own modality order instead (modalities= picks one of several variants, else the one the folder's files satisfy); category and method are validated whenever given (ValueError / KeyError with a hint). The set of files never depends on the method - labels are per dataset - and every path is absolute. So labels=mtb.labels_for(ds) goes straight into evaluate (one entry, or several with each cell's file of origin as the batch); labels_for(ds)["cty"] picks one file. Raises FileNotFoundError if the dataset directory is absent.

docs.title: mtb.data.fetch
docs.text:
mtb.data.fetch(*datasets: str, data_path=None, quiet: bool = False) -> Path

Ensure the named reference datasets exist locally, downloading them from the repository's release assets if needed (D11 11 MB, D28 137 MB, D45 290 MB, D46 97 MB, D52 179 MB); idempotent, returns the data root. An unknown id raises with the ids available.

docs.title: mtb.data.fetch_outputs
docs.text:
mtb.data.fetch_outputs(dataset: str, methods: list[str] | None = None, *,
                       data_path=None, quiet: bool = False) -> Path

Download the benchmark host's real run_all output tree for a tutorial dataset - exactly what run_all writes and load_batch reads: batch_result.json, long.csv, summary.csv and one <method>_<dataset>/ folder with the method's embedding.h5 - and return the dataset folder, <data_path>/outputs/<dataset>/. The URLs come from the shipped manifest multibench/engine/output_urls.json ({"<dataset>": "<url>"}; the four tutorial datasets D11, D28, D46, D52 under the data-v1 release, outputs-<dataset>.tar.gz). Idempotent (a folder that already holds batch_result.json is not downloaded again), traversal-safe extraction, prints what it downloads unless quiet. methods restricts the tree the returned folder is read with - an unknown name raises KeyError listing the methods in the tree; the function returns the dataset folder either way, and load_batch(path, methods=...) applies the filter. An unknown dataset raises ValueError listing the manifest's ids. This is what the category tutorials stand in on a host without the method environments (real embeddings, so their evaluate cell scores one):

>>> res = mtb.load_batch(mtb.data.fetch_outputs("D11"), methods=["Matilda", "sciPENN", "scMM"])
>>> res.summary[["method", "status", "run_sec"]]          # the benchmark host's statuses and times

docs.title: mtb.plot.bubble
docs.text:
mtb.plot.bubble(long_df, *, metrics=None, methods=None, order=None, aggregate="dataset",
                cmap=None, title=None, save=None, show_language=True,
                require_complete=False, overall="rank", na="warn") -> matplotlib.figure.Figure

Paper-style bubble table of a tidy long results frame: methods are rows (best first), metrics are columns grouped into the benchmark's task families, each family preceded by an Overall bar. A plain function - help(mtb.plot.bubble) shows this signature. mtb.plot.__all__ is bubble, bar, build_table, BubbleTable, FAMILIES, CLUSTERING_METRICS, BATCH_METRICS; the numbers half,

mtb.plot.build_table(long_df: pd.DataFrame, *, metrics=None, methods=None, order=None,
                     aggregate: str = "dataset", require_complete: bool = False, overall: str = "rank",
                     na: str = "warn") -> BubbleTable

returns a BubbleTable with methods in row order, overall, matrix - the min-max fills, norm is the same frame -, raw, ranks - the per-column max-ranks concatenated over the family blocks in figure order, index == methods, n = best -, blocks, aggregate, overall_basis, datasets, coverage, method_datasets, category, needs_labels and na_cells (every selector keyword-only: build_table(df, ["ARI"]) raises TypeError). The drawing half, mtb.plot.render(table, cmap=, title=, show_language=), stays importable but is not in __all__. Circle radius is 0.85 * sqrt(rank / n) with n the methods scored in that column.

Parameters

  • long_df (pd.DataFrame) - columns method, metric, value at least (what to_long, load_results and BatchResult.long return); dataset is needed for aggregate="summary". Concatenate frames to compare your method with the benchmark's.
  • metrics (list[str] | None) - metric codes to show, drawn in THIS order within each family block; alias tolerant; an unknown code raises ValueError naming the metrics present.
  • methods (list[str] | None) - methods to show (exact / canonical / case-insensitive); unknown -> ValueError with a hint.
  • order (list[str] | None) - row order for the listed methods; unlisted methods follow, best first. Only reorders, never filters; unknown names raise.
  • aggregate (str) - "dataset" (default; raw values, circles; several datasets are averaged per method with a UserWarning and dataset-tagged row labels) or "summary" (within-dataset max-ranks averaged over datasets, bars; a UserWarning lists methods missing from some datasets).
  • cmap (str | None) - colormap overriding the FIRST family's palette (default blues / greens / purples per family).
  • title (str | None), save (str | None) - figure title; fig.savefig(save, bbox_inches="tight"), format by suffix.
  • show_language (bool) - Py / R chip per row (? for methods not in the registry) and an L badge for label-consuming methods, judged by the variants of the FRAME's category (a needs_labels column in the frame - long["needs_labels"] = True for your own supervised method - is honoured first; inconsistent values for one method raise); a key line under the legends explains the chips (Py / R = language · L = consumes cell-type labels (supervised) · ? = not a registry method).
  • na (str) - what to do when a method lacks a metric: its Overall averages the ranks of the metrics it HAS and that column's ranks count only the methods scored in it; "warn" (default) reports each such method once per build (YukiNet: DR and clustering Overall over 3 of 4 metrics (cLISI n/a), kept as table.na_cells), "skip" is silent, "raise" refuses an incomplete frame.
  • require_complete (bool) - with "summary": restrict to methods present in EVERY dataset (ValueError if none is).
  • overall (str) - "rank" (default: minmax(mean over metrics of max-rank(mean over datasets of within-dataset max-rank)), absence = rank 0) or "mean_overall" (mean over datasets of minmax(mean over metrics of within-dataset max-rank), absence skipped). Pass the same value to plot.bar for the same ordering; the formula in use is printed on the figure.

Raises ValueError for missing columns (with a hint when the frame looks like evaluate()'s wide output), unknown names, duplicate (method[, dataset], metric) rows (they would be silently averaged), bad aggregate / overall.

docs.title: mtb.plot.bar
docs.text:
mtb.plot.bar(long_df, *, metrics=None, group: str | None = None, top: int | None = None,
             title: str | None = None, cmap: str = "Blues", show_datasets: bool = True,
             save: str | None = None, overall: str = "mean_overall") -> matplotlib.figure.Figure

Bar chart of each method's across-dataset Overall score. group="clustering" / "batch" selects a metric family (the benchmark's two summary panels; "Greens" is forced for batch); top keeps the N best; show_datasets overlays one dot per dataset behind each bar (under overall="mean_overall", where whiskers are the SD of the per-dataset scores). mtb.plot.CLUSTERING_METRICS and mtb.plot.BATCH_METRICS are the two family constants.

docs.title: mtb.eval.*
docs.text: mtb.eval.evaluate and mtb.eval.to_long are the same functions as mtb.evaluate and mtb.to_long (the namespace's __all__); mtb.eval.io.read_labels(path, column=None) is the header-aware label reader both use (column x / the only column / the last of two behind an index column; ValueError naming the columns when ambiguous - pick one with its column= and pass the array to evaluate).

docs.title: mtb.io.*
docs.text: The input-format adapter to and from the canonical scMultiBench .h5 (an HDF5 file with matrix/data of shape features x cells, plus matrix/features and matrix/barcodes; float64, gzip-compressed, chunked, like the shipped files). mtb.io.__all__ is export_dataset, to_canonical, read_canonical, normalize_peak_names; the 0.2 from_mudata is folded into export_dataset and write_labels is private (AttributeError for both - a label CSV is one header line x and one label per cell, pd.Series(labels, name="x").to_csv(path, index=False)).

docs.title: mtb.io.export_dataset
docs.text:
mtb.io.export_dataset(data, dataset_dir: Path | str, *, rna="X", adt=None, atac=None,
                      atac_kind: str | None = None, labels=None, batch=None,
                      dtype: str = "float64", compression: str | None = "gzip",
                      category: str | None = None, adt_names: list | None = None) -> Path

Write an AnnData / MuData as a canonical benchmark dataset folder - rna.h5, adt.h5, atac_peak.h5 (+ a hard-linked atac.h5) or atac_gas.h5, and cty.csv - so that mtb.scan(name, data_path=dataset_dir.parent) and run_all work on your own data. rna / adt / atac take a selector string - 'X', 'obsm:<key>', 'layer:<key>', 'mod:<name>' (MuData; optionally 'mod:<name>.obsm:<key>') - OR an object: an AnnData, a DataFrame or a 2-D array; labels / batch take a selector or a Series / sequence. When data is a MuData the bare modality NAME works too (rna="rna", atac="atac" = mdata.mod[name].X) and labels / batch accept '<mod>:<obs column>' (labels="rna:celltype") - what the 0.2 from_mudata did:

mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, "data/MYMULTIOME", rna="rna", atac="atac", atac_kind="peak",
                      labels="rna:celltype", category="vertical")   # -> rna.h5, atac.h5, cty.csv

Every modality is re-indexed to one master obs_names order (that of data), and a modality whose barcode set differs raises ValueError (all modalities of one dataset must cover the same cells). ADT feature names come from the DataFrame columns / AnnData var_names / uns["<obsm key>_names"]; a bare array falls back to feature_0.. with a UserWarning - pass adt_names=[...]. None skips the modality. atac_kind is required with atac: 'peak' (chr:start-end features) or 'gene_activity' (-> atac_gas.h5 only, so the gene-activity role never silently falls back to a peak matrix); a warning is raised when the feature names contradict the declared kind. labels is 'obs:<col>' (or 'mod:<name>.obs:<col>') -> cty.csv (header x); batch (same grammar) splits the cells per batch value and writes the numbered rna1.h5 / adt1.h5 / cty1.csv ... layout instead. category (keyword-only) fixes the ATAC filename for the layout you target: "vertical" writes plain atac.h5 for BOTH atac_kind values - the vertical (paired multiome) methods read the atac role and never atac_peak.h5 / atac_gas.h5; the representation is recorded nowhere on disk, so feed the one method_info(m)["atac"] wants; "diagonal" / "mosaic" / "cross" keep atac_peak.h5 / atac_gas.h5 (no atac.h5 link); None keeps today's names. All matrices are cells x features and written transposed; sparse matrices are streamed. Returns dataset_dir.

docs.title: mtb.io.to_canonical
docs.text:
mtb.io.to_canonical(src, out: Path | str | None = None, modality: str | None = None, convert: bool = True, *,
                    layer: str | None = None, obsm: str | None = None, mod: str | None = None,
                    dtype: str = "float64", compression: str | None = "gzip", block: int = 1024,
                    category: str | None = None, feature_names: list | None = None) -> Path

Convert src to a canonical .h5 and return its path. src is an AnnData, a MuData (mod= required), or a path to .h5ad / .h5mu / .csv / .tsv (cells x features) / .loom / a canonical .h5 (passed through untouched). out is the output file, or an existing directory when modality is given - then the canonical filename (rna.h5, adt.h5, atac_peak.h5, atac_gas.h5, atac.h5) is appended. modality (rna | adt | atac | atac_peak | atac_gas; aliases protein, peak, gas / gene_activity) is validated, warns when ATAC feature names contradict the role, and with modality='adt' on an AnnData that has obsm keys requires obsm= / layer= to say where the protein matrix is. category="vertical" (keyword-only) makes an ATAC role write plain atac.h5 whatever the representation - the file the vertical methods read (to_canonical(atac, d, modality="peak") alone writes atac_peak.h5, which no vertical variant opens); the other categories and None keep atac_peak.h5 / atac_gas.h5 / atac.h5. feature_names= overrides the feature names written to matrix/features. convert=False means "never write" (non-canonical input raises). A missing src path raises FileNotFoundError naming the path and the current directory; an .h5 without matrix/data raises ValueError listing the keys it found (and flags a top-level data as a method OUTPUT, not an input). Sparse matrices are streamed without densifying, but matrix/data is stored dense (features x cells x 8 B uncompressed): above mtb.io.DENSE_WARN_BYTES (1 GB) a UserWarning states the size and the two mitigations - filter to HVGs / informative peaks first, or dtype='float32', which halves it.

docs.title: mtb.io.read_canonical
docs.text:
mtb.io.read_canonical(path: Path | str, sparse: bool | None = None) -> AnnData

Read a canonical .h5 back into an AnnData (cells x genes), restoring var_names from matrix/features and obs_names from matrix/barcodes (sparse=None auto-selects CSR below 50 % density).

docs.title: mtb.catalog.*
docs.text: Typed views of the benchmark's metadata CSVs, plus the canonicalisers used throughout the API.

docs.title: mtb.catalog.methods
docs.text:
mtb.catalog.methods(files_dir: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

The methods table (method, canonical_id, language, deep_learning, atac, output, needs_labels, list-valued categories / tasks); needs_labels / atac / categories / tasks are overlaid from the registry at call time so they cannot drift. Defaults to config.DEFAULT.files_path.

docs.title: mtb.catalog.datasets
docs.text:
mtb.catalog.datasets(files_dir: Path | str | None = None, *, category: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

The datasets table: the union of the paper's dataset table and every id with a stored result table (80 rows: the 71 catalogued ids plus nine that exist only as result tables - the D11s / D28s / D45s / D52s re-run subsamples, D24, SD7-SD10 - appended in natural order). Columns: dataset (id), simulated (true for ids beginning SD), category and has_results (filled from the shipped result tree at call time), plus the paper-derived assay / tissue / n_cells / n_batches / source columns, currently empty.

docs.title: mtb.catalog.metrics
docs.text:
mtb.catalog.metrics(files_dir: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

The metric-details table (whitespace-normalised column names).

docs.title: mtb.catalog.canonical_id
docs.text:
mtb.catalog.canonical_id(name: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> str

Return the canonical registry method id for any known display or result-dir spelling (e.g. "seurat v5" -> "Seurat_v5", "mofa+" -> "MOFA2"), case-folded against the registry ("scipenn" -> "sciPENN"). An unknown name is returned unchanged; strict=True raises KeyError with a did-you-mean hint instead (what load_results uses). mtb.catalog.known_metrics() lists the metric codes the tables can carry (the ten scIB codes plus PCR).

docs.title: mtb.catalog.canonical_metric
docs.text:
mtb.catalog.canonical_metric(code: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> str | None

Canonicalise a raw metric short-code (e.g. "ari" -> "ARI", "kbet" -> "kBET"); returns None for blank or empty codes (strict=True raises ValueError for an unknown code instead of returning it unchanged).

docs.title: mtb.config.Config
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Config:
    result_path: Path   # stored benchmark metric tables (scib_metric/ + rerun/)
    files_path: Path    # metadata CSVs (method/dataset/metric)
    repo_path: Path     # reference scMultiBench repo (method entrypoints)
    data_path: Path     # resolved input datasets
    envs_dir: Path      # where the method env prefixes live (packed archives unpack here)
    leiden_flavor: str  # "igraph" (default) or "leidenalg": evaluate's Leiden sweep

Resolved filesystem paths and two knobs. Override any field to point at custom locations. A module-level default instance is exposed as mtb.config.DEFAULT; callers may replace its fields in place (mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir = Path("/scratch/envs"), mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "leidenalg"). mtb.config.__all__ is Config, DEFAULT - the on-disk token maps (category_folder, metric_set_dir) are internal since 0.3.0 (still importable, hidden from dir(mtb.config)).

  • envs_dir - resolution order: the MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR environment variable; else the first writable conda envs dir when a conda / mamba binary is found on PATH; else ~/.cache/multibench/envs. env install --packed extracts archives into <envs_dir>/<env>, and env_prefix looks there first.
  • leiden_flavor - the scanpy Leiden flavor behind evaluate's resolution sweep (ARI / NMI / iF1): "igraph" (default; n_iterations=2, directed=False, measured 7.7x faster on 20k cells) or "leidenalg". mtb.eval.scib.leiden_sweep(emb, flavor=None) takes the same token per call; None reads this field.

docs.title: mtb.env.*
docs.text: Helpers for the environments that mtb.run orchestrates - mtb.env.__all__ is status, plan, install, doctor, recipe, each behind the multibench env subcommand of the same name; everything else in the module is CLI plumbing (importable, not advertised). The CLI is the everyday surface - multibench env doctor (what exists / is missing, with the exact install line for the gaps), multibench env plan --category vertical (the envs with their download / disk sizes and a # total), multibench env status (installed? plus a build-difficulty tag), multibench env install --methods X --packed --run (a dry run until --run; --packed downloads prebuilt archives and falls back to the lockfile build; --flavor auto|cpu|gpu picks the CPU-only or the CUDA archive, see archive flavours). The environments are linux-64 conda envs: on any other host the CLI prints a warning: ... linux-64 ... line first and env install --run refuses unless --force (force=True on mtb.env.install); dry runs work everywhere.

docs.title: Run modes: prefix and conda
docs.text:
Nothing needs a conda binary once an env's prefix is on disk. Per call, run (and so run_all, and the command column of scan) picks one of two wrappers for the built command <cmd>:

  • prefix - the default whenever env_prefix(env) exists. The argv is bash -c '<activate>; exec "$@"' -- <cmd>, where <activate> sets CONDA_PREFIX=<prefix>, CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV=<env>, PATH=<prefix>/bin:$PATH and sources every <prefix>/etc/conda/activate.d/*.sh (the R environments ship six, and they assume CONDA_PREFIX is set), so python / Rscript in <cmd> resolve inside the env.
  • conda - the fallback when no prefix is on disk but a conda / mamba binary is found: conda run -n <env> <cmd>, the only mode before 0.3.0's speed round.

MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=conda|prefix forces one; prefix forced with no prefix on disk raises OSError naming envs_dir and mtb.env.install. cmd_template= still overrides everything. The pty opt-in and the process-group kill are the same in both modes.

mtb.env.env_prefix(env: str) -> Path | None

The prefix run would activate for a registry env name: <envs_dir>/<env> when it contains bin/ (envs_dir = mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir); else, when conda is found, the prefix conda reports for that name; else None. installed_envs() and scan's env_ok gate count an env as installed exactly when this is not None - with or without conda.

docs.title: mtb.env.status
docs.text:
mtb.env.status(conda: str | None = None, *, as_frame: bool = False)

One row per registry method - {method, env, group, own_env, exists, has_lock, difficulty, verified_working, has_recipe, flavor} (as_frame=True -> a DataFrame); difficulty is the build tag env status prints (easy, old-scvi, old-tensorflow, R, verified, blocked-script, unknown; the legend goes to stderr); flavor is cpu / gpu when the installed env came from a packed archive (the <prefix>/.multibench_flavor record, see archive flavours), else None.

docs.title: mtb.env.plan
docs.text:
mtb.env.plan(category: str | None = None, methods: list[str] | None = None, *,
             as_frame: bool = False)

Which envs to build to cover a set of methods - [{env, shared, methods, availability, flavor}], one entry per distinct env listing the methods it serves (build these few envs instead of one per method); availability is benchmark-host-only when every method the env serves needs an unpublished script - only SPIRAL's spiral_environment today (the env builds, the method still cannot run off the benchmark host) - else public; flavor is the installed archive's flavour when recorded (cpu / gpu), else None. The CLI adds the packed-archive download size and the unpacked size per env (from the shipped multibench/engine/packed_sizes.json snapshot; ? = not measured) for the archive --flavor selects, and a # total line naming the flavour it summed.

docs.title: mtb.env.install
docs.text:
mtb.env.install(methods: list[str] | None = None, *, category: str | None = None,
                packed: bool = True, dry_run: bool = True, conda: str | None = None,
                force: bool = False, flavor: str = "auto") -> list[dict]

The Python face of multibench env install (the CLI calls this function). Builds the install plan for the selection - methods and/or category, neither = the whole benchmark - and returns one dict per env: {env, methods, exists, has_lock, cmds, state, packed_url, archive_bytes, unpacked_bytes, flavor}, where cmds are the argv lists a lockfile build runs. dry_run=True (default) returns the plan and creates nothing - state is have, packed archive published (an archive exists; packed_url / archive_bytes say which and how big), no archive - lockfile build, build(dry-run) (packed=False), or NO-LOCK; dry_run=False installs - the packed archive when packed and one is published (falling back to the lockfile build when the download fails), the lockfile build otherwise - and state becomes PACKED, BUILD, have or NO-LOCK. Environments that already exist are skipped, so an interrupted install resumes. On a non-linux-64 host a real run raises unless force=True. conda overrides the conda executable. No conda binary is needed for the packed path: a packed archive is downloaded, extracted into <envs_dir>/<env> (Config.envs_dir) and finished with the archive's own bin/conda-unpack (run with <prefix>/bin first on PATH - the archive carries its own python); the linux-64 guard and the traversal-safe extraction apply as before. A lockfile build on a host without conda / mamba raises RuntimeError BEFORE any download: no conda/mamba on this host; <env> has a packed archive - pass packed=True when an archive exists (packed=False was asked), ... has no packed archive - install conda first when none does.

flavor picks the packed archive per env - "gpu" (the CUDA build every env has), "cpu" (the <env>-cpu archive where published, else the CUDA build with one UserWarning) or "auto" (default: cpu when host_has_gpu is false, else gpu); anything else raises ValueError listing the three. The dry-run rows' packed_url / archive_bytes / unpacked_bytes follow the flavour (a null size in the snapshot reads as unknown, like a missing entry), and flavor says which archive each env would get (cpu / gpu after the per-env fallback) - or, for an env already installed, the flavour recorded for it (None when it was built from a lockfile). packed=False rows carry flavor=None.

>>> mtb.env.install(["Matilda"])[0]          # dry run: the plan for one method's env, on a GPU host
{'env': 'matilda', 'methods': ['Matilda'], 'exists': False, 'has_lock': True, 'cmds': [[...], [...], [...]],
 'state': 'packed archive published', 'packed_url': 'https://zenodo.org/records/21928889/files/matilda.tar.gz?download=1',
 'archive_bytes': 3043807507, 'unpacked_bytes': None, 'flavor': 'gpu'}
>>> mtb.env.install(["Matilda"], flavor="cpu")[0]["packed_url"]   # the CPU archive, once published
'https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench/releases/download/envs-v1/matilda-cpu.tar.gz'

docs.title: Archive flavours: cpu and gpu
docs.text:
The tutorial torch environments (env_sciPENN, matilda, scmb_scjoint, scmb_torch, scmb_scmm2) are published twice: the CUDA build under the env name and a CPU-only build under <env>-cpu, the same environment without the CUDA libraries and roughly 3-4x smaller. Whatever the flavour, the archive is unpacked into <envs_dir>/<env> - the env name never changes, so run, scan and the registry are untouched - and install_packed writes the flavour that landed to <prefix>/.multibench_flavor (one word), which status / plan / doctor return as flavor and the CLI prints as flavor=cpu. A CPU archive counts as published once packed_urls.json lists it and packed_sizes.json carries its measured archive_bytes (the maintainer tool records that after the upload); a listed-but-unmeasured entry is a placeholder for an archive that is not there yet, and every flavour keeps taking the CUDA build until it is.

mtb.env.host_has_gpu() -> bool

Is an NVIDIA GPU visible on this host - True when nvidia-smi is on PATH and nvidia-smi -L exits 0 listing at least one device, or when /proc/driver/nvidia/version exists; nothing else counts (a torch install or a CUDA library on disk says nothing about the machine). Cached per process (host_has_gpu.cache_clear() re-probes). This is the whole of the flavor="auto" decision. Importable from mtb.env, not part of mtb.env.__all__.

docs.title: GPU or CPU?
docs.text: The archive flavour is about the environment; whether a method can run without a GPU is about its script, and the registry records that per method from the script's source. method_info(m)["cpu_params"] lists the command-line values that turn CUDA off in a script that has it on by default ({'use_cuda': ''} for scJoint - argparse type=bool, so only the empty string is false - and {'device': 'cpu'} for scMDC); when host_has_gpu() is False, run merges them into params unless you set the key yourself, and run(..., dry_run=True) / scan(...)["command"] show the merged flags. method_info(m)["requires_gpu"] is True for a script that calls CUDA unconditionally (scBridge, moETM, SMILE, sciCAN, UnitedNet, iPOLNG, SPIRAL; gpu_evidence is the file:line); without a GPU run raises OSError before launching and scan / run_all report the sentence in env_reason. Every other method either has no CUDA call or falls back to CPU on its own (torch.cuda.is_available()), and scMM / scMVP / scMSI keep the CPU treatment the registry already gave them (--no_cuda / CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""). On a GPU host none of this applies. The tutorial in Run a method shows the calls.

docs.title: mtb.env.doctor
docs.text:
mtb.env.doctor(category: str | None = None, methods: list[str] | None = None,
               conda: str | None = None, *, as_frame: bool = False)

Preflight: per env needed to run the methods, is it present and is a lockfile available to build it - [{env, methods, exists, has_lock, flavor}], coverage-sorted (as_frame=True -> a DataFrame; flavor = the installed archive's flavour when recorded, else None). The CLI legend: [x] installed, [L] missing with a lockfile ready, [!] missing and no lockfile, then the multibench env install ... line for the gaps.

docs.title: mtb.env.recipe
docs.text:
mtb.env.recipe(method: str) -> dict
